LESSON: SELECTED SURAHS • AL- FATIHA • AN-NAAS • AL-FALAQ • AL-IKHLAS • AL- MASAD • AN-NASR • AL- KAFIRUN

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Qur’an
Topic 1.1: Selected Surahs • Al- Fatiha • An-Naas • Al-Falaq • Al-Ikhlas • Al- Masad • An-Nasr • Al- Kafirun
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 21

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Selected Surahs • Al- Fatiha • An-Naas • Al-Falaq • Al-Ikhlas • Al- Masad • An-Nasr • Al- Kafirun, part of Qur’an in Grade 4 ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION.

Key inquiry question: Why do we recite suratul - Fatiha in every swalah? 2. Which surahs do Muslims recite before going to bed?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. listen to the teacher/resource person or from a digital device recitation of the selected surahs,
2. discuss the basic meaning of the selected surahs, in groups, and write in their notebook,
3. listen to recorded translation of the selected surahs from a digital device,
4. sort verses of the selected surahs with their corresponding meaning using digital devices/flash cards/ match individually/groups. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Selected Surahs • Al- Fatiha • An-Naas • Al-Falaq • Al-Ikhlas • Al- Masad • An-Nasr • Al- Kafirun together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: the skills of listening and teamwork are enhanced as learners discuss the basic meaning

and lessons of the selected surah through group discussion.

• Digital literacy: the skill of connecting using digital technology is enhanced through use of digital devices to listen to

recorded translation of the selected surahs.

• Creativity and imagination: the skill of making connection is enhanced as learners sort verses of the selected surahs with

their corresponding meaning.

2

Values:
• Responsibility: enhanced as learners sort verses of the selected surahs with their corresponding meaning using digital

devices/flash cards/ match individually/groups

• Unity: cooperation is enhanced as learners work together in groups.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Citizenship: Social cohesion as learners discuss the lessons learnt from the selected surahs, in pairs or small groups.

Links to other Learning Areas:
As learners read selected surahs and relate reading skills in English and Kiswahili.
